description: baseline

Baseline spends 73.8% of GPU time in the unblocked scalar Householder panel kernel (no tensor cores) on the dominant batch640-n512 / batch60-n1024 shapes. Replace it with RECURSIVE blocked Householder QR (Elmroth-Gustavson): factor a narrow panel with a custom CUDA C++ kernel (panel in shared memory), recurse to halve panel width, build the block reflector T, and apply the WY update (I - V T V^T)^T to the trailing submatrix as large cublasGemmStridedBatched / cublasGemmEx calls so the bulk of FLOPs run on tensor cores. Emit compact (H,tau) reflectors natively. Tune panel width nb; route n off the supported grid to a torch.geqrf fallback (off-grid-n guard).

Blocked Householder QR (nb=64) with WY trailing update via TF32 batched bmm. Mathematically correct (well-conditioned + rankdef/clustered/nearcollinear pass), ~1.85x faster on batch640-n512 prototype. But TF32 trailing GEMM loses precision on ill-conditioned wide-dynamic-range inputs: band/rowscale/mixed n=512 fail factor residual by ~1.5x (scaled ~26-30 vs allowed). Need FP32-accurate GEMM (disable TF32, or 3xTF32 emulation).

Blocked Householder QR (nb=64) with WY trailing update via FP32 batched bmm; blocked path for n in {176,352,512,1024}, route n in {32,2048,4096} and all off-grid n to torch.geqrf. All 22 test shapes + kernelguard + 3 guards (differential/invariance/offgrid) PASS. Geomean 75523us vs baseline 111805us = 1.48x. Key finding: tensor cores (TF32) give NO speedup over FP32 SIMT for the thin K=nb=64 trailing GEMMs AND fail ill-conditioned accuracy gate; the win is the blocked structure replacing the 74% scalar panel kernel, kept in FP32.

Custom CUDA panel-QR kernel (one CTA per matrix, panel in shared memory, block-parallel Householder) to replace the slow cuSOLVER tall-panel geqrf (measured 120ms for 512x64 batch640 vs 3.9ms for 256x64 - a 30x cliff above m=256). Build failed: at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream missing header; also note validate.sh bans 'stream' in submission.py so must launch on default stream (no stream arg).

Custom panel kernel correct on n=176/352/512 incl band/rowscale/mixed (FP32, no TF32 accuracy issue). But crashes cudaErrorInvalidValue on n=1024: first panel is 1024x32 = 128KB shared, exceeds the sm_120 100KB opt-in limit. Need adaptive nb so tallest panel (height=n) fits shared: n=1024 needs nb<=24 (96KB) or nb=16 (64KB).

Custom on-chip panel-QR kernel (one CTA/matrix, panel in shared mem, block-parallel Householder w/ warp-shuffle reductions; adaptive nb so tallest panel fits 100KB shared: nb=32 for n<=512, nb=24 for n=1024) + WY blocked trailing GEMM (FP32 bmm). Eliminates the cuSOLVER tall-panel cliff. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Geomean 14493us vs baseline 111805us = 7.71x. Per-shape: n=512 ~30us (was 506), n=1024 ~27us (was 171), n=176 1.7ms, n=352 3.7ms. n=2048(69ms)/n=4096(40ms) still route to geqrf and now dominate geomean.

Extended custom blocked path to n=2048 (nb=12, 1.20x vs geqrf); n=4096 stays on geqrf (small nb forced makes it 6-8x slower). Refined nb selection to largest nb<=32 fitting shared. All tests+guards PASS. Geomean 14354us (7.79x). Phase breakdown now shows trailing WY GEMM is 63%, custom panel kernel 26-32%, T-build 5-11% — bottleneck shifted to the trailing bmm.

2-level blocking: factor each wide block (NB_W=128 for n<=512, 192 for n>=1024) via narrow nb-wide custom-kernel panels with small in-block WY updates, then apply the whole wide block's WY to the far-trailing columns as ONE large GEMM. Amortizes the dominant trailing-GEMM over a wider block (fewer launches, larger contraction). Fixed a double-application bug (in-block _apply_wy must bound columns to wend, caught by standalone correctness before benchmark). All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Geomean 11116us vs baseline 111805us = 10.06x. n=512 22.2ms, n=1024 17.2ms, n=2048 40ms (1.72x), n=4096 still geqrf.

Fused the panel kernel's reflector application: instead of nb separate block reductions per Householder step (one per trailing column, each with 2 syncs -> O(nb^2) syncs/matrix), each thread now accumulates partial dots for ALL trailing columns in registers, then 2 syncs/step produce all w_k at once. Panel kernel 512x32 dropped to 744us. All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. Geomean 9733us vs baseline 111805us = 11.49x. n=512 19.6ms, n=1024 14.8ms, n=2048 38.7ms.

Brief exhausted. Best: 9733us geomean = 11.49x over baseline 111805us (commit 2cfa7b04, iter8). Faithfully realized the brief: blocked Householder QR with WY trailing update via batched GEMM (torch.bmm->cuBLAS), custom on-chip CUDA panel kernel (one CTA/matrix, panel in shared mem, fused block-parallel Householder), block reflector T, compact (H,tau) native, off-grid n->geqrf. WHAT WORKED, in impact order: (1) The custom panel kernel was the decisive win (7.71x at iter5): cuSOLVER's batched geqrf has a ~30x cliff for tall panels (512x64 batch640 = 120ms vs 256x64 = 3.9ms), so the scalar panel was 98% of a naive blocked QR; the on-chip per-matrix kernel sidesteps it. (2) 2-level blocking (iter7, +1.3x): factor each wide block (NB_W=128 for n<=512, 192 for n>=1024) via narrow nb-wide custom panels with small in-block WY updates, then ONE wide trailing GEMM to the far-trailing cols -- the wide GEMM is far more efficient than nb-wide ones. (3) Fusing the panel kernel's reflector application across all trailing columns (iter8, +1.15x): 2 syncs/Householder-step instead of O(nb). WHAT DID NOT WORK: TENSOR CORES DO NOT HELP on this problem/hardware -- tested twice (full-trailing TF32 at iter1, wide-GEMM-only TF32 later): TF32 batched GEMM is ~equal speed to FP32 SIMT (the WY trailing GEMMs have small contraction dim K=nb, and even the wide K=128 case showed 1.02x) AND TF32 fails the ill-conditioned factor-residual gate (band/rowscale/mixed n=512). 3xTF32 emulation was 10x slower. So the kernel is pure FP32 and the win is purely structural. On-chip T construction (larft in the panel kernel) was SLOWER than PyTorch _make_T (gram via cuBLAS bmm + solve_triangular) because the on-chip gram parallelizes poorly over m -- reverted. nb=48 panels and BLOCK-size dispatch were neutral-to-worse (reverted). n=4096 stays on geqrf (forced small nb makes blocking 6-8x slower); n=2048 is on the custom path (1.72x). SUGGESTIONS FOR NEXT BRIEF: current phase split for n=512 is panel 36% / wide-trailing-GEMM 30% / Tbuild 16% / in-block 15%. The wide _make_T (jb=128) is ~615us x4 -- a cheaper wide-T (e.g. compose from narrow Ts via cross-grams, or a custom T kernel that parallelizes the gram over m) could cut Tbuild. The in-block updates (15%) are narrow GEMMs that might be foldable. The trailing GEMM (30%) looks near FP32 SIMT peak. A fundamentally different angle (brief 1's CholeskyQR normal-equations path) may beat Householder on the well-conditioned-majority shapes if its robustness gate can be met. NOTE: nsys benchmark-mode profiles are dominated (~68%) by eval.py's recheck=True FP64 checker GEMMs (cutlass d884gemm), which do NOT count toward the leaderboard mean -- use the per-phase CUDA-event breakdown in my logs instead. Leaderboard submission is the manager's responsibility.

Brief 1 (fix n=2048/n=4096 underfill) exhausted with NO improvement over parent iter8 (9733us); left HEAD identical to 2cfa7b04. Real per-shape breakdown: at n=2048(b8)/n=4096(b2) the wide trailing GEMM is only 4-9% of time; the cost is the MANY tiny make_T + in-block WY ops (batch=2-8, underfilled) forced by the small nb that the 100KB shared cap imposes (nb=12 at n=2048, nb=6 at n=4096). ncu confirms underfill: panel kernel launches just 8 CTAs (b8) at 1.4% SM throughput / 16.6% occupancy -- but the brief forbids fanning the panel (single-CTA, no cross-CTA sync), and the panel is not the dominant cost. WHAT I TRIED, ALL SLOWER: (a) reshape trailing GEMM bmm->looped-mm: helps only at batch=2 per-call (n=4096) but the nb=6 op-count still dominates; neutral at batch=8. (b) larger nb via cuSOLVER panel (nb=32-128): WORSE (68-74ms at n=2048 vs current 40ms; cuSOLVER panel slow). CONCLUSION: n=2048 is at its structural floor (1.72x, 40ms; current 2-level custom already beats every alternative); n=4096 MUST stay on geqrf (custom path with forced nb=6 is ~4x slower). The blocked-Householder lineage cannot fix these two shapes because the fix requires a fast LARGE-nb tall panel factorization, which the 100KB shared cap forbids (and global-memory / cuSOLVER large-nb panels are both slower). SUGGESTIONS: (1) A TSQR (communication-avoiding) panel that splits panel height across CTAs could both raise SM-fill AND enable larger nb, but it changes the reflector structure -- emitting compact (H,tau) from a TSQR tree is nontrivial and is a whole brief of its own. (2) For n=4096 b2 specifically, geqrf is the floor for Householder; only a fundamentally different algorithm (W1's CholeskyQR, if its robustness gate passes on the ill-conditioned benchmark shapes) might beat it. Your blocked kernel is at its FP32 floor; n=2048 (1.72x) and n=4096 (geqrf, 1.0x) stayed unfixable ONLY because the 100KB shared cap forces tiny nb. TSQR (communication-avoiding QR) is the Householder-lane fix and keeps you DISTINCT from workers 1/2 (normal-equations CholeskyQR): the panel is tall-skinny (m x nb), so split its HEIGHT across many CTAs -- each CTA does a short tall-skinny Householder on a row-block (a LARGER nb now fits in shared), then a Householder reduction tree merges the per-block R's. This fills the 188 SMs (batch 2-8 -> many CTAs/matrix) AND enables large nb. TSQR is unconditionally backward-stable, so UNLIKE worker 2's CholeskyQR-n=4096 (which falls back to geqrf at 1.0x on the ill-conditioned cases) it needs NO robustness fallback -- and since the benchmark RANKS conditioning robustness, TSQR is the only path that can beat 1.0x on ill-conditioned n=4096. PRIMARY target n=2048 (you own it, ~1.72x->~3x is +4.7% geomean alone); n=4096 as stretch/hedge. CRITICAL RISK + GUARDRAIL: a TSQR tree yields a FACTORED Q, not flat compact (H,tau); reconstructing the single geqrf-compatible (H,tau) (orhr_col-style, proven in this run) can cost as much as the factorization. So in iteration 0-1 MEASURE the reconstruction cost IN ISOLATION first; if reconstruction is >= the factorization it replaces, ABANDON TSQR and instead do RECURSIVE blocked Householder (Elmroth-Gustavson): recurse the panel (factor left half, WY-update right half, factor right half) so the on-chip working set is a sub-panel not full n x nb, growing effective nb at n=2048/4096 without the 100KB cap -- this stays in the Householder lane AND emits compact (H,tau) NATIVELY (no reconstruction). Keep all other dispatch branches unchanged; FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards green; profile to confirm SMs-in-use and nb both rise on n=2048/4096.

Brief 3 (TSQR / recursive-Householder for n=2048/4096) exhausted: NO improvement; HEAD stays at parent c99b68a8 (9375us, 11.93x). Followed the guardrail exactly. STEP 1 (measure TSQR reconstruction in isolation): the orhr_col reconstruction of compact (H,tau) from an orthonormal Q is structurally a blocked modified-LU (getrfnp) of Q -- W1's branch confirms this (custom getrfnp panel kernel + batched-GEMM trailing update, SAME 99KB shared cap / tiny-nb constraint as a QR panel). Measured the reconstruction cost (cuSOLVER lu_factor proxy, same FLOP class) vs my factorization: n=2048 recon=51.6ms = 1.45x the 35.5ms factorization; n=4096 recon=86.5ms = 2.13x the 40.6ms factorization. Since reconstruction ALONE exceeds the factorization, TSQR (= TSQR-factor + reconstruct) is strictly worse than my current direct blocked QR -> ABANDONED TSQR per the guardrail. STEP 2 (pivot to recursive blocked Householder / Elmroth-Gustavson): implemented + VERIFIED CORRECT (all test shapes pass, emits compact (H,tau) natively, zero reconstruction) -- recurse the wide block (factor left half, WY-update right half, factor right half, combine T=[[T1,-T1(V1^T V2)T2],[0,T2]]). But it is SLOWER: n=2048 0.74x (48.6ms vs 35.9ms current), n=4096 0.13-0.19x (216ms vs 40.5ms). Root cause: the recursive T-combine needs a cross-gram V1^T V2 over the full m=2048/4096 ROWS at EVERY recursion level -- those extra batched GEMMs (at batch 2-8) cost far more than the restructured in-block updates save. The base panel nb is STILL capped at 12/6 by the 100KB shared limit (recursion restructures the inter-panel updates but does NOT grow the base nb, contrary to the brief's hope). CONCLUSION (now confirmed across briefs 1 AND 3): n=2048 (1.72x, 35ms via my 2-level) and n=4096 (geqrf, 1.0x) are at the Householder-lane FLOOR. The low batch (2-8) underfills everything; the shared cap forces tiny nb; every restructuring (bigger-nb global/cuSOLVER panel, single-level, TSQR+orhr_col, recursive E-G) adds more cost than it removes. n=4096 ill-conditioned robustness: TSQR is unconditionally stable but its reconstruction cost sinks it, so it cannot beat geqrf's 1.0x here either -- the ill-conditioned-n=4096 ranking advantage the brief hoped for is unreachable in the Householder lane. RECOMMENDATION: stop attacking n=2048/4096 in the Householder lane; n=4096 belongs to W1's CholeskyQR (only it forms Q cheaply enough to make the orhr_col reconstruction affordable). Global best stays the combine lineage; my c99b68a8 narrow-T win is the contribution to fold in. Parent profile at c99b68a8 already on disk.
